page: Microsoft Azure E4ns_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Env6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

This server type runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include local SSD storage, meaning all storage operations rely on external Premium Storage. The instance is designed for network-intensive workloads, though it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mixed profile. Single-core CPU performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1916.18 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.08 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3927.87. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measuring 31.34 GB/sec and 23.07 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET performance are positioned in the lower tier, while static web serving throughput remains average at 7.48 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the E4ns_v6 is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high multi-core compute density. It is suited for moderate database caching, light web serving, single-threaded data processing, and small-scale language model inference, where its AMX instructions can be leveraged.
